edges.label: Shared reporting-reform agenda: ASRS and FAA pilot reporting
edges.note: The NASA study team recommended enhancing the Aviation Safety Reporting System for commercial pilot UAP reporting; ASA performs the equivalent intake function for aircrew outside the chain of command.

edges.label: Created in direct response to the reporting failure the encounters exposed
edges.note: Graves's testimony ties the founding to the fact that after his squadron's safety report 'there was no official acknowledgement of the incident and no further mechanism to report the sightings.'

a.label: Fleet Forces Command 'URGENT SAFETY OF FLIGHT ISSUE' Email (Jan 2015, recalled)

edges.label: Command-level reaction to the encounter series
edges.note: The message describes exactly the problem Graves's squadron reported - repeated near-midairs with unidentified objects in working airspace - and was withdrawn within 24 hours.

a.label: ODNI Preliminary Assessment: Unidentified Aerial Phenomena (25 June 2021)

edges.label: Official confirmation of the stigma ASA exists to route around
edges.note: The assessment concedes 'disparagement associated with observing UAP, reporting it, or attempting to discuss it with colleagues' - the condition that made a civilian aircrew nonprofit necessary.

edges.label: Founder and Executive Director
edges.note: Graves founded the organisation in 2022 to build the aircrew reporting channel the Navy did not provide, and appeared before Congress in that capacity in July 2023.

b.label: House Oversight hearing, 26 July 2023 - 'Unidentified Anomalous Phenomena: Implications on National Security, Public Safety, and Government Transparency'

edges.label: sworn witness
edges.note: Graves testified alongside David Fravor and David Grusch; his written statement is in the committee record.

edges.label: VFA-11 aircrew during the 2014-2015 encounter series
edges.note: Graves testified in writing that his squadron 'began witnessing advanced UAP demonstrating complex maneuvers on a regular basis' after the AESA radar upgrade.

edges.label: Squadron at the centre of the Atlantic encounter series
edges.note: Graves names VFA-11 and Warning Area W-72 in sworn testimony as the locus of the encounters and the near-midair.

edges.label: Flag-officer corroboration of the safety-reporting failure ASA was built around
edges.note: Gallaudet's recalled-email account and Graves's unacknowledged squadron safety report describe the same broken machinery from opposite ends of the chain of command.

edges.label: Navy F/A-18F pilot turned first active-duty-era witness before Congress
edges.note: In his own words: 'My name is Ryan "FOBS" Graves and I am a former F-18 pilot with over a decade of service in the U.S. Navy, including two deployments in Operation Enduring Freedom and Operation Inherent Resolve.' He joined the Navy in 2009, describes the encounters in the W-72 warning area, and states 'I founded Americans for Safe Aerospace to create a center of support, research, and public education for aircrew impacted by UAP encounters', reporting nearly 5,000 members and more than 30 witnesses working with the organisation.

edges.label: East Coast UAP encounters reported by Roosevelt-deployed Navy aircrew
edges.note: Two of the three videos the Department released in April 2020 are dated January 2015, and Graves's testimony places his squadron's encounters in the W-72 warning area off the east coast, beginning more than a decade before he testified: 'my squadron began witnessing advanced UAP demonstrating complex maneuvers on a regular basis'. Tier 2 because neither primary document names the USS Theodore Roosevelt. The carrier association is well attested elsewhere; it is not in the two documents cited here.

a.label: Warning Area W-72, off Virginia Beach

edges.label: Site of the near-midair that anchors the safety case
edges.note: Restricted training airspace ten miles east of Virginia Beach where two F/A-18Fs 100 feet apart took evasive action around a stationary cube-in-sphere object.
